tone_statements.citation: 经典 (Jīng Diǎn). 2020. 碧约哈尼语双音节化的类型及产生机制 [Types and formation mechanism of disyllabification in Biyo Hani]. 民族语文 Minzu Yuwen 2020(1): 76-82. Open PDF:https://mzyw.ajcass.com/Admin/UploadFile/Issue/34arszde.pdf
tone_statements.quote: 以、为前缀的双音节和四音节词，在 3187 个词中分别有 219 条和 249 条，多为名词。 选择还是作为前缀，主要依据是后一音节元音的舌位。后一音节元音为舌面前元音时，往 往与前缀搭配；后一音节元音为舌面后元音或舌尖元音时，多与前缀搭配。和音节还有 有高平、中平和低降调三个声调。声调的选择也与后一音节的声调高低相关。后一音节声调 高，前缀也多为高平或中平调；后一音节声调低，前缀则多为低降或中平调。
tone_statements.translation: Disyllabic and quadrisyllabic words with the prefixes a- and X- number 219 and 249 respectively among the 3187 words, mostly nouns. Whether a- or X- is chosen as the prefix depends mainly on the tongue position of the following syllable's vowel: when the following syllable has a front vowel it usually combines with the a- prefix; when it has a back or apical vowel it mostly combines with the X- prefix. The a and X syllables also have three tones: high level, mid level and low falling. The choice of tone likewise correlates with the height of the following syllable's tone: if the following syllable's tone is high, the prefix is mostly high level or mid level; if the following syllable's tone is low, the prefix is mostly low falling or mid level.
tone_statements.locator: p. 77, section 二(一) 单音节附加前缀构成双音节词
tone_statements.summary: 3 tones named (high level, mid level, low falling); syllable TBU; prefix tone harmonizes with root-syllable tone height.

sources.citation: Hansson, Inga-Lill. 1989. A comparison of Akha, Hani, Khatu and Pijɔ. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 12(1): 6-91.
sources.note: Pijɔ (= Biyue, one Mojiang informant, p. 7) phoneme tables p. 8: three non-laryngealized tones High/Mid/Low plus laryngealized Mid/Low; 'The tonal systems of Khatu and Pijɔ correspond exactly to Akha and Hani. The low tone is in all of them slightly falling. Some differences in the tones may depend on sandhi rules, which remain to be worked out.' No word 'stress' or 'accent' anywhere in the scanned pp. 6-25 (rest of article is correspondence sets).
